transcript:
Meeting header: Date/Time: 2026-08-03 16:00 UTC | Duration: 55 minutes | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Samira (QuasarLink Head of Partnerships), Evan (QuasarLink Cloud Architect), Priya (QuasarLink Security), Liam (Product)

Summary: Quick joint solution workshop to align on marketplace listing requirements, network/KMS integration patterns for QuasarLink's managed gateway, and a pilot plan for Dedicated capacity + canary routing. Action items captured and an initial pilot week proposed.

Topics: marketplace onboarding checklist, listing assets, VPC peering and SSO, KMS/keys and audit logs, benchmarking plan (latency/cost), quantization/compat tradeoffs, rollout & canary policies.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you squeezing this in. agenda is lightweight, want to make sure we have runway for the network and security bits which Evan and Priya will help with.
[00:16] Samira: yeah thanks Jordan, we've got folks on product and security so we can make decisions. primary ask is: how quickly can we get a listing live and a small pilot so we can demonstrate joint value to our marketplace customers.
[00:30] Maya: hi all, Maya here, i'll be the SE on this. quick note - there are two paths: hosted API listing (fast) vs Dedicated listing with reserved capacity for a managed gateway flow. they have different onboarding asks.
[00:45] Evan: when you say managed gateway flow can you clarify — we run QuasarLink's gateway in customer vnets and want to front Redwood models for inference, is that the right mental model?
[00:57] Maya: yes that's right, basically you can route requests to Redwood Private / Dedicated behind VPC peering or through a secure ingress. we commonly see customers choose Dedicated for predictable throughput.
[01:12] Liam: what's the timeline if we pick Dedicated? like how long to provision and run a pilot?
[01:20] Jordan: typically we can stand up a Dedicated pool in 10-14 business days once contractual/PO and network bits are done. pilot (canary roll) we try to schedule within 1-2 weeks after that depending on test scope.
[01:34] Priya: on security we need to map SOC2 / logs / KMS usage. can you talk about where audit logs live and how long retention is?
[01:44] Maya: good question. audit logs for Private deployments are pushed to customer telemetry endpoints or S3 buckets; retention is configurable but by default we keep 90 days in the console and you can export longer. note - export tooling is still in the new runbook, but it's supported.
[01:58] Samira: can QuasarLink use their own KMS? we have a requirement for customer-managed keys for some enterprise tenants.
[02:06] Maya: yes, we have KMS integrations for Dedicated and Private — customer-managed KMS is supported, includes HSM-backed keys if needed. small caveat: we need the key policy and the KMS ARN during onboarding so we can set up decrypt permissions for the runtime.
[02:22] Evan: ok we'll share the ARN. regarding networking: do you require VPC peering, or can we use a private link-type approach? our infra team prefers peering but we can be flexible.
[02:34] Jordan: both are options. peering is straightforward for most clouds; for marketplace listing we usually document both patterns. PrivateLink-type offerings (or equivalent) are supported but we need to validate route tables and NAT behavior.
[02:48] Maya: one note — if you plan to push large batch workloads, we recommend configuring an autoscaling policy with a burst pool. we'll advise in the perf runs.
[02:58] Samira: perfect. about listing assets — what do you need from us for the marketplace catalog page?
[03:05] Jordan: we need a short blurb (50-120 words), logo assets (svg + 2 raster sizes), 2-3 screenshots or architecture diagrams, pricing tiers, and an optional joint-solution whitepaper. i'll share a checklist.
[03:20] Samira: i'll take that. we'll also want the joint go-to-market blurb — co-branded one pager.
[03:25] Jordan: yes we'll help. i'll add a draft to the shared folder.
[03:30] [04:12] Maya: moving to perf — can you share expected qps, typical prompt sizes and percentiles for latency SLOs? that'll drive model selection and quantization tradeoffs.
[04:22] Evan: for our initial pilot, 50-100 rps, typical prompt ~120 tokens, top P use cases include conversation routing and summarization ops. latency target is 200-400ms p95 if possible; cost is a factor so we want a balance.
[04:38] Maya: got it. latency target is ambitious for open models at that token length but with quantized variants and optimized kernels we can approach it on Dedicated with the right instance class. we should run a quick benchmark with a sample workload.
[04:52] Liam: are there models you recommend off the shelf for this? we prefer open models for cost and auditability.
[04:58] Maya: we usually recommend Redwood-curated open models that have been verified for throughput — i'll send a short matrix. also tradeoffs: int8 quantization reduces cost but sometimes increases latency variance; KV-cache warmup behavior matters for chat-style workloads.
[05:14] Evan: KV-cache — sorry heard as kick V cache earlier in the notes?
[05:20] Maya: yes KV cache, sometimes transcription gets funny. it's key-value caching for autoregressive decoding state, reduces repeated prefix cost.
[05:28] [07:05] Priya: on compliance, we need a clear audit trail: who invoked which model, token logs, and data residency. can you confirm whether logs contain PII and if there's redaction?
[07:18] Jordan: logs capture metadata and token usage; payload logging is opt-in and we advise redaction. for regulated tenants we recommend turning off payload logging and exporting only aggregated usage metrics.
[07:30] Priya: ok please share the security runbook. also SAML/SSO for console access — is SSO supported for customer admins?
[07:39] Maya: yes SAML SSO is supported for Redwood Console; we'll need your IdP metadata file. RBAC model supports org-level roles and token-level scopes.
[07:50] Samira: for the marketplace listing approval there is a preflight checklist on their side; do you have any timing constraints or approval gates?
[07:59] Jordan: couple of typical gates: compliance signoff, billing/metering connector verification, and a short UAT with 2-3 customers. we can align timelines after we get your assets and network details.
[08:12] Evan: on billing we'd like metered per-1000 tokens; is the marketplace meter mapping straightforward?
[08:20] Jordan: we support per-token billing; the marketplace layer sometimes enforces their own SKU mapping — we will coordinate with your marketplace ops. there may be a slight delay for meter reconciliation but it's standard.
[08:34] [09:45] Maya: can we walk through the pilot test plan quickly? step 1: small canary using test traffic in alpha tenant; step 2: run 6-hour stability test with synthetic traffic; step 3: invite 2 internal beta customers; step 4: open to marketplace UAT.
[09:58] Evan: sounds good. do you provide an automated canary rollback if latency or errors spike?
[10:05] Maya: yes, our rollout tool supports canary policies and automatic fallback to a hosted variant if Dedicated capacity degrades. that'll be in the runbook. small note: routing policies require model variant mappings.
[10:20] Samira: we may want a banner in the console indicating the partnership and link to joint sales materials — possible?
[10:27] Jordan: yes totally — we can add a co-branded link on the listing and include a partner badge.
[10:33] [11:15] Liam: question on private deployment licensing — if clients want air-gapped installs via QuasarLink's appliance and Redwood runtime, what's typical model?
[11:25] Maya: for air-gapped on-prem we offer a Private package; there's an enterprise licensing add-on and a separate deployment playbook. it typically requires longer lead time for cert and KMS connectivity.
[11:36] Evan: ok we'll flag any customers that need on-prem.
[11:40] [13:02] Priya: can we confirm TLS termination expectations? who terminates TLS for inbound client traffic to the gateway and between gateway and Redwood runtime?
[13:12] Jordan: gateway should terminate client TLS; connections to Redwood runtime are mutual TLS or within peered VPC with security groups restricting 443. we recommend mTLS for extra layer.
[13:27] [14:00] Maya: i'll attach a sample security diagram and the mTLS cert rotation guidance.
[14:07] Samira: perfect. any blockers from legal side for joint listing?
[14:13] Jordan: usually we exchange a mutual marketing agreement and confirm logos and trademarks. legal approves the copy. should be straightforward.
[14:20] [20:00] Maya: quick note about quantization - if you need lower cost we can try int8 or mixed-precision; but we'll run model-quality guardrails using your prompt set. want to avoid regressions.
[20:15] Evan: we'll share a small prompt set — maybe 200 prompts across our main flows for evaluation.
[20:21] Maya: perfect, that will let us run quality/regression tests pre and post-quantization.
[20:30] [28:10] Jordan: circling back to timeline - if we get assets and network details this week, provisioning starts next week, pilot mid-August. that aligns with your internal events?
[28:22] Samira: yes mid-August is ideal. we'll prioritize assets and the sample workload.
[28:30] [36:40] Evan: one last technical Q — how do you handle model version pinning and rollbacks if a model update degrades quality?
[36:50] Maya: you can pin model versions per route; rollouts use canaries and we keep previous versions as fallbacks. we also support auto-fallback to a cheaper hosted variant if Dedicated goes unhealthy.
[36:58] Priya: will those fallback logs show which variant served each request? for audit?
[37:06] Maya: yes the trace includes model variant id, route id, latency, and error codes, which you can push to your telemetry.
[37:15] [45:00] Jordan: ok let's recap next steps and owners. Jordan will share the checklist and draft listing copy; Maya will send the perf runbook and quant configs; QuasarLink to provide VPC/CIDR, KMS ARN, and SAML metadata; schedule pilot for week of 2026-08-17.
[45:20] Samira: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[45:25] Jordan: thanks, i'll follow up with calendar invites and the shared folder link.
[45:30] [55:00] Meeting ended.
